name: clockwork_rings
description: a clock face of light on dark olive: a quasicircle Julia set's basin lit green-gold round a hot heart and ringed and spoked, concentric equipotential rings beyond it crossed by fine radial field lines, and small luminous gear discs riding the rings, more and smaller on every ring inwards

reference.made_with: a flame fractal (Apophysis-style), Wikimedia Commons, 'Chaos Clock - The Steampunk Spell-Shaper'

reuses: a quasicircle Julia set seen whole (z^d + c at the fixed point's multiplier |lam| < 1, arg near 0 or pi): its equipotentials are near-circles round the set and its field lines run out radially, the concentric structure the galleries lack (step 4's exception)
field smooth as two period sheets, one a step and four a step: the rings and the clock face's graduations
field_lines' lines channel outside, its angle divided and cut by a fine period sheet with no twist: the radial hairlines

two single bubble discs outside the set (gilded_orbs' unlatticed trap, bounded by largest and smallest): each pulls back as d discs a ring inwards, d times as many and smaller each ring, so the discs ride the rings and crowd to the set; each has a dim fill, a bright rim (the height inverted), spokes (its angle in a twelve-band sheet) and a hot middle

star_eye's lines channel inside: the arrival step inverted is the hot heart round the attracting fixed point, its angle cut into 36 spokes; the inside channel's bands ring each preimage of the fixed point
glow_filaments' falloff glows on de, softened (teal_filaments' 4e-4 screened core)
a fog of the inverted distance estimate by rank, and the tone pass at the reference's median and p10
notes: Added: nothing: period sheets on the smooth count for the rings, the `lines` angle for the hairlines, two single bubble discs whose pullbacks ride the rings, the `lines` channel inside for the lit and spoked basin. Its structure, concentric rings round a point, is one the galleries lack (measured): its locations are hand-placed (step 4's exception)

Lessons: The eighteenth style is a flame-fractal clock: concentric glowing rings round a green-gold core, small luminous discs riding the rings, fine radial lines, on dark olive. It went in with **no new primitive**, on `star_eye`'s quasicircle Julia sets seen whole. Three lessons. **Outside a quasicircle the escape-time fields are already a clock face**: its equipotentials are near-circles round the set, so a period sheet on the smooth count draws the rings (a second at a quarter period the graduations), and its field lines run out radially, so the `lines` angle cut fine with no twist draws the hairlines. **A single disc outside the set rides the rings**: its pullbacks lie on the equipotentials, `d` discs a ring, `d` times as many and smaller each ring inwards, crowding to the set, so the riding discs are also the frame's proof that zooming in shows more; two discs at different angles double them without a lattice, which would pack the whole frame. **Light a basin from its attracting point, not its convergence count**: the `inside` count peaks at every preimage of the fixed point, so as a glow it lit a dozen equal hot spots in a flat olive blob; the `lines` channel's arrival step inverted lights the basin outwards from the fixed point, its angle cut into 36 spokes, while the `inside` bands ring each preimage, smaller and smaller towards the set. Seats whose basin is a smooth disc with few preimages still read as one object and were dropped by eye. The structure was measured: a 320x200 rank render of the smooth count, scored by the share of its variance a function of the radius alone explains (best of 25 centres in the frame's middle third), reads median 0.23 over 200 `final139_general` seats (none at 0.7, five at 0.5) against median 0.82 at `star_eye`'s twelve quasicircle seats. Seats come from the fixed point's multiplier `λ` (`|λ| < 1`, `arg λ` near 0 or π so the basin does not spiral): `d·z^(d−1) = λ`, `c = z − z^d`. All 40 drafts and the eleven full renders hold the reference's balance.
